rgb: The camera wearer stands on an unfinished interior staircase looking downward into a bright ground-floor entryway with white walls, a tiled floor, an open doorway, and a window in the background within arm's reach, about 0.5 to 1.5 metres away. Directly below but far and out of reach (3 to 5 metres) are concrete steps, a vertical metal baluster post on the step below, and a sloped stainless-steel handrail on the right, while the ascending upper flight of stairs and an overhanging landing wall sit far to the left. A person in a yellow plaid shirt and dark trousers stands at the base of the stairs to the lower right, roughly 1.5 to 2.5 metres below and in front of the camera wearer, positioned 3 to 5 metres from and out of reach of the bottom stair post and surrounding floor debris. Across the tiled floor below, about 2 to 4 metres from the wearer and 0.5 to 2 metres from the standing person, lie scattered construction materials including cardboard, electrical cords, a handheld power tool, bags, and bundles of long metal pipes and orange-wrapped rods to the left. The standing person faces away from the stairs and looks upward away from the camera wearer in frame 1 and toward the upper left in frame 4, while his head and upper torso are cropped out by the right frame edge in frames 2 and 5 and completely out of view in frame 3 as the camera pans left toward the overhanging stairwell wall and then pans back right.
depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer standing high on an indoor staircase looking down into a lower landing within arm's reach (0.5 to 1.5 metres away, rendered dark) bordered by a right wall, an overhanging central wall/upper flight on the left, and descending steps in the bottom foreground. In frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, a standing man in a yellow plaid shirt is below and to the right at roughly 2 to 2.5 metres from the wearer, with a vertical metal railing post on the steps about 3 to 5 metres below and in front of the wearer and out of reach of the standing man's right hand. A diagonal metal handrail in the bottom-right of frames 1, 4, and 5 and the overhanging stairwell wall on the left of frames 2, 3, and 5 appear bright white at 3 to 5 metres and out of reach of the wearer, while in frame 3 the camera pans left so the overhanging wall and ascending upper stairs at 3 to 5 metres occlude the standing man. Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns their head left toward the upper stairwell between frames 1 and 3 and back to the right in frames 4 and 5, causing the distant handrail and standing man to exit the right edge in frame 3 before re-entering and shifting right again in frame 5. The depth map makes the steep vertical drop, step-by-step distance gradient, and far separation of the overhanging stairwell wall and foreground handrail much clearer than the RGB image alone, but it is unreliable within 1.5 metres where the floor clutter, tools, metal pipes, and a crouching person at the top-center (within arm's reach at ~0.5 to 1.5 metres, ~2.5 metres behind the standing man) vanish into uniform black.
segmentation: The segmentation map isolates very few elements of the stairwell scene on a black background, detecting only the standing man on the right (`person`, ~2 to 2.5 metres below and right of the camera wearer) in frames 1 and 4, and the nearby crouching figure (`person`, within arm's reach at ~0.5 to 1.5 metres in the upper-middle background, ~2.5 metres from the standing man) in frame 1. In frame 1, the standing man faces his body away from the bottom-left stairs while turning his head up to look away from the camera wearer, whereas in frame 4 he stands behind the foreground diagonal handrail (which partially occludes his lower legs) and looks forward/left away from the stairs and toward the wearer. Also in frame 1, a blue-and-yellow flattened cardboard box on the floor within arm's reach, ~0.5 to 1.5 metres below the wearer and ~3 to 5 metres to the left of and out of reach of the standing man, is segmented, and the same box is segmented again in frame 5 as the camera turns left. While the mask silhouettes in frame 1 help separate the nearby crouching figure and the standing man's torso contour from the visually cluttered floor in the RGB strip, the map is highly unreliable overall. It completely misses the standing man when he is partially cropped at the right frame edge in frames 2 and 5, misses the crouching person in frames 2 through 5, fails to segment the stairs, walls, railings, pipes, or tools 3 to 5 metres from and out of reach of either person, and misclassifies the floor cardboard box as a `laptop` in frame 1 and a `book` in frame 5.
pose: The pose map renders 2D yellow body skeletons against a black background for the standing man (~2 to 2.5 metres below and to the right of the camera wearer) in frames 1 and 4, and a small cluster of keypoints on the lower landing (within arm's reach at ~0.5 to 1.5 metres below and slightly right of center) in frame 2. In frame 1, the skeleton's wide shoulder-to-hip trapezoid and facial keypoints show the man facing his torso away from the stairs to his right while angling his head upward away from the camera wearer, with his right wrist extending down 3 to 5 metres from and out of reach of the lower stair post and floor box and his legs clipped at the knees. After disappearing in frames 2 and 3 as the wearer turns left and the man is cropped out of view on the right, his skeleton reappears in frame 4 with a narrower torso profile and head keypoints oriented up and to the left, showing that he has turned his head toward the camera wearer and away from the staircase while his lower legs are occluded behind the foreground handrail. This skeletal geometry makes the change in the standing man's torso twist and head orientation between frames 1 and 4 easier to read than in the high-angle RGB view alone. However, the map is unreliable across the rest of the sequence: it completely misses the standing man when his head is cropped out at the right border in frames 2 and 5, fails to detect the nearby crouching person within arm's reach at ~0.5 to 1.5 metres in all frames (apart from spurious keypoints 3 to 5 metres from and out of reach of floor clutter in frame 2), and detects no magenta hand skeletons or camera-wearer limbs anywhere.
